The five TCM events that stood here (MET 9.8 to 13.85) had no source and were removed.

Sriharikota, India, 2008-10-22. Chandrayaan-1 — India's first lunar mission. Carried 11 instruments including NASA's M³ (Moon Mineralogy Mapper) that would later be credited with the first detection of widespread water on the Moon.
Series of phasing perigee burns lifted Chandrayaan-1 from Earth orbit to lunar transfer — same energy-saving Earth-orbit raising strategy ISRO would reuse on Mangalyaan.

2008-11-08. Captured into a 504 × 7,502 km polar orbit, lowered to 100 km on 2008-11-12. Released the Moon Impact Probe on 2008-11-14, which hard-landed at Shackleton crater near the south pole — making India the 5th national space agency to reach the lunar surface. Mission ended 2009-08-29 (10 months) when its power supply units failed. NASA's M³ data was later analysed to discover lunar surface water at >40 ppm.

Perigees after the first burn are not published there and are drawn at 255 km. Ecliptic plane; orbit phase schematic.
India's first lunar mission; confirmed widespread water on the Moon

ISRO's first interplanetary spacecraft. The orbiter delivered the Moon Impact Probe to the lunar surface — the first Indian object on another world — and carried 11 instruments from 6 countries. NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3) instrument, hosted on Chandrayaan-1, made the discovery that rewrote textbooks: water molecules are widespread across the lunar surface, not just locked in polar shadowed craters. The mission ended abruptly in August 2009 when ISRO lost communication with the spacecraft.
Moon Impact Probe targeted hard-landing near south pole.
